title: Braves’ Ronald Acuña Jr. exits early with left hamstring tightness in road opener
content:
CHICAGO — Ronald Acuña Jr. exited the Atlanta Braves’ series-opening 6-5 extra-innings loss against the Chicago White Sox in the fourth inning with left hamstring tightness, the club announced Tuesday.

The Braves outfielder was limping as he ran down the first-base line on a groundball. He was replaced by Eli White.

It is the same hamstring Acuña injured earlier this season, requiring a stint on the injured list.

Entering Tuesday, Acuña was hitting .254 with seven home runs and a .798 OPS over 52 games.

Should Acuña require another stay on the IL, he will join a group that includes catchers Drake Baldwin and Sean Murphy, centerfielder Michael Harris II and a slew of pitchers. Even after Tuesday’s loss, the Braves have MLB’s best record at 45-22.
